title: Transfer Learning
subtitle: Feature Extraction, Fine-tuning, and Adaptation
content:
🎯 What You'll Be Able to Do

  • Explain why transfer learning works and when it doesn't
  • Choose between feature extraction and fine-tuning
  • Use a pretrained backbone for vision and NLP tasks
  • Avoid catastrophic forgetting and label leakage

Before you start: Complete Lessons 8 (TensorFlow) and 10 (Embeddings). You should know what a neural network layer and an embedding are.

🧭 The Core Idea

Train a big model once on a big generic dataset. Then transfer what it learned to your task with a small dataset and a small budget.

Why this works: early layers learn general features (edges, n-grams) that transfer across tasks; only late layers need task-specific tuning.

Two main flavors:

  • Feature extraction - freeze the pretrained backbone, train only a new head. Cheap, decent, works on tiny datasets.
  • Fine-tuning - unfreeze (some of) the backbone and continue training with a low learning rate. More expressive, needs more data and care.

📐 When Transfer Learning Helps (and When It Doesn't)

It helps when:

  • Your target dataset is small.
  • The source domain is similar to the target (e.g., ImageNet -> medical imaging keeps working longer than ImageNet -> audio spectrograms).
  • The source model is general-purpose (foundation model).

It doesn't help as much when:

  • Your target domain is very different from any pretrained model's training.
  • You have plenty of target data - then training from scratch can match or beat transfer.
  • The task is novel and there's no learned backbone that has useful features.

🖼️ Vision: Feature Extraction with a Pretrained Backbone

Feature extraction with MobileNetV3 (TensorFlow/Keras) 

import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow.keras import layers, models

# Last verified: 2025-07
# Load a pretrained backbone, freeze it, train a new head on your dataset
backbone = tf.keras.applications.MobileNetV3Small(
    input_shape=(224, 224, 3),
    include_top=False,  # drop the 1000-class ImageNet head
    weights="imagenet"
)
backbone.trainable = False  # feature-extraction mode

model = models.Sequential([
    backbone,
    layers.GlobalAveragePooling2D(),
    layers.Dropout(0.2),
    layers.Dense(64, activation="relu"),
    layers.Dense(num_target_classes, activation="softmax")
])

model.compile(optimizer="adam", loss="sparse_categorical_crossentropy", metrics=["accuracy"])
model.fit(train_ds, validation_data=val_ds, epochs=5)
import tensorflow as tf from tensorflow.keras import layers, models # Last verified: 2025-07 # Load a pretrained backbone, freeze it, train a new head on your dataset backbone = tf.keras.applications.MobileNetV3Small( input_shape=(224, 224, 3), include_top=False, # drop the 1000-class ImageNet head weights="imagenet" ) backbone.trainable = False # feature-extraction mode model = models.Sequential([ backbone, layers.GlobalAveragePooling2D(), layers.Dropout(0.2), layers.Dense(64, activation="relu"), layers.Dense(num_target_classes, activation="softmax") ]) model.compile(optimizer="adam", loss="sparse_categorical_crossentropy", metrics=["accuracy"]) model.fit(train_ds, validation_data=val_ds, epochs=5)

🔧 Fine-tuning the Same Backbone

After feature extraction has converged, unfreeze the last few layers of the backbone and resume training at a much lower learning rate.

Fine-tuning the last 20 backbone layers 

# Unfreeze the last 20 layers of the backbone and fine-tune
backbone.trainable = True
for layer in backbone.layers[:-20]:
    layer.trainable = False

# Crucially: use a LOW learning rate for fine-tuning
model.compile(
    optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(1e-5),  # 10x lower than default
    loss="sparse_categorical_crossentropy",
    metrics=["accuracy"]
)
model.fit(train_ds, validation_data=val_ds, epochs=5)
# Unfreeze the last 20 layers of the backbone and fine-tune backbone.trainable = True for layer in backbone.layers[:-20]: layer.trainable = False # Crucially: use a LOW learning rate for fine-tuning model.compile( optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(1e-5), # 10x lower than default loss="sparse_categorical_crossentropy", metrics=["accuracy"] ) model.fit(train_ds, validation_data=val_ds, epochs=5)

Why low LR: the backbone is already good; we want to nudge it toward our task, not erase what it knows (catastrophic forgetting).

🨄 NLP: Three Levels of Transfer

  1. Use the pretrained model as-is (embeddings + classifier) - feature extraction.
  2. Full fine-tune a BERT/encoder - unfreeze everything, train head + backbone with 2e-5 LR for 2-3 epochs.
  3. PEFT (LoRA/QLoRA) - efficient adapter fine-tuning. See Lesson 14 (Fine-tuning & PEFT) for the modern recipe.
Fine-tuning DistilBERT for binary classification 

from transformers import AutoTokenizer, TFAutoModelForSequenceClassification

# Feature-extraction style: load a pretrained encoder and a fresh head
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("distilbert/distilbert-base-uncased")
model = TFAutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(
    "distilbert/distilbert-base-uncased", num_labels=2
)

# Full fine-tune (small LR, few epochs to avoid forgetting)
from tensorflow.keras.optimizers import Adam
model.compile(optimizer=Adam(2e-5), loss=model.compute_loss, metrics=["accuracy"])
model.fit(train_ds, validation_data=val_ds, epochs=2)
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, TFAutoModelForSequenceClassification # Feature-extraction style: load a pretrained encoder and a fresh head tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("distilbert/distilbert-base-uncased") model = TFAutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained( "distilbert/distilbert-base-uncased", num_labels=2 ) # Full fine-tune (small LR, few epochs to avoid forgetting) from tensorflow.keras.optimizers import Adam model.compile(optimizer=Adam(2e-5), loss=model.compute_loss, metrics=["accuracy"]) model.fit(train_ds, validation_data=val_ds, epochs=2)

⚠️ Pitfalls

  • Label leakage - if your fine-tuning set sneaks test examples in, your "transfer" looks better than it is. Strict splits only.
  • Catastrophic forgetting - fine-tuning too aggressively erases general skills. Mitigate with low LR, few epochs, or PEFT.
  • Wrong preprocessing - the backbone was trained on images normalized to ImageNet stats. Use the same preprocessing at inference, or quality tanks.
  • Variance in adapted features - freezing the backbone on a tiny target dataset can underfit; check validation across multiple random seeds.

✅ Decision Shortcut

  1. Start with feature extraction (frozen backbone + a trainable head). 5 epochs.
  2. If accuracy is too low, try fine-tuning the last ~10% of the backbone at 10x lower LR.
  3. If still too low, gradually unfreeze more or move to PEFT (Lesson 14).
  4. If you have millions of target and the source domain differs, consider training from scratch.

💻 Try It Yourself

questions.question: You have 500 labeled images and want to classify a medical condition. Best first attempt?

options.text: Feature extraction with a pretrained ImageNet backbone and a trainable head
Train a CNN from scratch on the 500 images
Use an LLM on image captions
Hand-craft features with HOG and SVM

questions.explanation: With small target data, feature extraction (frozen backbone + fresh head) is the cheapest and typically best first move.

questions.question: After feature extraction converges, you unfreeze the last 10 layers and keep training. What LR should you use?

options.text: An LR 10x lower than feature-extraction LR (often ~1e-5) to avoid erasing pretrained features
The same LR - momentum carries over
A higher LR to escape the local minimum
LR doesn't matter for fine-tuning

questions.explanation: Fine-tuning a pretrained backbone at high LR causes catastrophic forgetting. Use ~1e-5 for ~2-3 epochs.

questions.question: Why does the same ImageNet-trained backbone give terrible results on audio spectrograms?

options.text: Domain shift - ImageNet features (edges, textures) don't transfer to spectrogram patterns
ImageNet models can't process 2D inputs
Spectrograms need a different loss function
Audio can't be embedded at all

questions.explanation: Transfer learning only helps when source and target domains share useful features. ImageNet features don't transfer well to audio spectrograms.

questions.question: You trained your classifier on a backbone pretrained on ImageNet but forgot to apply ImageNet preprocessing at inference. What happens?

options.text: Quality tanks - the backbone expects the same input distribution it was trained on
Nothing - backbones are robust to preprocessing
It becomes faster
It becomes slower

questions.explanation: Pretrained models assume the exact preprocessing used at training. ImageNet uses specific mean/std normalization. Apply the same at inference.

questions.question: Which is the modern efficient alternative to full fine-tuning of a 7B-parameter LLM?

options.text: PEFT (LoRA / QLoRA) - freeze the base, train small adapter matrices
Train a new 7B model from scratch
Use only feature extraction (frozen model + linear head)
Switch to a smaller model and train from scratch

questions.explanation: PEFT freezes the base and trains tiny adapter weights - memory and storage drop dramatically. See Lesson 14 for the recipe.
